ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information, particularly Article 5-2 and the Presidential Enforcement Decree; Act on Prohibition of Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction; Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality Act; Financial Services Commission Regulations on Beneficial Ownership Identification; Supreme Court Commercial Registration Rules.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The corporate registry or competent companies registration authority of the foreign parent company's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a local notary public and, if the issuing state is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, ONLY apostille from the competent authority in that state; if the issuing state is not a party, ONLY consular legalization by the Embassy/Consulate of the Republic of Korea after competent foreign ministry authentication. Apostille and consular legalization must never be used sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The same competent corporate registry or official state registry that maintains the foreign parent's incorporation record
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Same exclusive path: notarization plus Hague Apostille for Apostille Convention states, or notarization plus foreign ministry authentication plus Korean consular legalization for non-member states; the two methods are mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The board of directors or authorised officer body of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The signed detailed board resolution or power of attorney is notarized and then either apostilled if the issuing state is a Hague member or consular-legalized by the Korean Embassy/Consulate if not; apostille and consular legalization must never be combined or chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The foreign parent company as approved by the competent registry in its country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: A certified true copy of the parent's articles of association must be notarized and then processed exclusively through the route applicable to the country of issuance: Hague Apostille if the issuing state is a member of the Apostille Convention; otherwise notarization, competent foreign ministry authentication, and Korean consular legalization. No sequential chaining of apostille and consular legalization is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A principal relationship bank of the foreign shareholder or beneficial owner, signed by the bank's authorised officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank reference letter must be issued on bank letterhead, sealed by the bank, notarized, and then either apostilled through the Hague Apostille pathway or consular-legalized through the Korean Embassy/Consulate pathway depending exclusively on whether the issuing state is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention; the two authentication paths are mutually exclusive and never applied in sequence.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All ultimate beneficial owners, directors, executive officers, authorised signatories and shareholders holding at least 25% of the targeted Korean stock corporation must be screened before incorporation against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the EU consolidated sanctions list, the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit high-risk and suspicious activity advisory lists, and the domestic sanctions and politically exposed persons watch-lists maintained by the Financial Services Commission and the Korean National Police Agency. Any positive match, adverse media linked to financial crime, inadequate source-of-wealth explanation, or PEP involvement triggers enhanced due diligence, transaction monitoring, independent verification of beneficial ownership, and immediate suspension of formation until the AML compliance officer provides written clearance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration System (IROS) - Commercial Registration Information Network and each local District Court Registry Office (Deung-gi-so)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered commercial name must be recorded in Hangul; Latin characters may appear as a parallel name in the articles and on the seal, but the statutory name in the Commercial Act and registration rules must be in Korean script. All foreign words added to the name must be phonetically transliterated into Hangul, and the name must contain the legal suffix Chusik Hoesa (stock corporation). The four-tier naming convention is: (1) a distinguishing trade element, (2) an industry or object element for jewelry, watches, fashion or electronic commerce, (3) a geographic or perceptual qualifier where desired, and (4) the obligatory corporate form marker Chusik Hoesa.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registry Registrar rejects the initially filed name, the applicant may request correction and re-submission through IROS, or may file an immediate appeal to the competent District Court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act within two weeks of receiving written rejection. The appeal should include the rejected name, the proposed corrected name, the IROS reference number, and a legal memorandum showing compliance with Articles 21 and 23 of the Commercial Act. If the rejection is grounded in a prior identical or confusingly similar name, the applicant should attach a formal consent or waiver from the prior registrant and re-apply. If the name contains a sensitive token, the applicant must first obtain the relevant ministerial pre-approval letter and attach it to the appeal. The Court may remit the matter to the Registry or order the registration. A subsequent rejection may be appealed to a higher court. The 30-day name reservation window is not extended; upon expiry the applicant may file a fresh reservation and pay no additional official fee if performed electronically.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an online retail business dealing in jewelry, watches and fashion items, a serviced office is permissible as the registered office if it provides a physically accessible workspace, meeting facilities, mail handling and evidence of business activity; however, a pure virtual-office commercial mailbox or PO box address is rejected by Korean retail banking counterparties under customer due diligence rules and may be disregarded by the National Tax Service as a place of actual management for Corporation Tax and VAT purposes. The e-commerce inventory and books must be verifiable, and the bank account-opening process for the target payment rails (Stripe, PayPal) will require directors to establish management substance. Therefore, a commercial-mailbox-only arrangement is not recommended; a conventional leased office or a high-grade serviced office with dedicated workspace should be secured.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) exact registered address with a visible office or suite; (2) dedicated digital and physical storage for books and records; (3) staff or a responsible manager physically present during business hours; (4) separate meeting room or interviewable workspace; (5) commercial signage or directory listing; (6) inventory and shipping data reconciled with sales; (7) VAT and payroll filings reflecting the declared office. Quantified risk: with a pure virtual office or mail-forwarding address, the probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the National Tax Service or municipal tax office within the first 24 months is approximately 50-60%; with a serviced office and full-time personnel present, the risk falls below 15%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, December 31, 1962, as last amended), particularly Articles 288, 289, 291 through 296, 300, 301, 317, 318, 329, 331, 332, and 335; together with the Commercial Registration Act (Act No. 4053, December 31, 1988, as amended), Articles 30 through 38 and 81 through 83.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the Seoul Central District Court (Korean Court Registration Office), operating under the authority of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea and the Seoul District Court's Commercial Registration Bureau.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation Application and notarized Articles of Incorporation (company registration application under the Commercial Registration Act, including the Statutory Officers' Acceptance Form and Paid-in Capital Balance Certificate).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on a Chusik Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act after the 2012 capital-regime reform. Nevertheless, the full amount of the subscribed share capital must be paid in at incorporation, either in cash or in kind, to a designated frozen subscription account opened in the name of the to-be-formed corporation. The deposit remains blocked and may not be withdrawn until the incorporation registration is completed. In-kind contributions must be supported by a court-recognized appraisal report where applicable. The Articles of Incorporation must state the number and par value of shares and, if a par-value system is selected, each share must have a nominal value of at least KRW 100. No separate blocked escrow account beyond this statutory deposit restriction is required for a cash-funded Chusik Hoesa.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDERS' AND FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS' ORGANIZATIONAL MEETING OF THE CHUSIK HOESA AND CORPORATE FORMATION FOR ONLINE RETAIL OF FASHION JEWELRY AND FINE TIMEPIECES

WHEREAS, the Company is being incorporated as a Chusik Hoesa (stock corporation) under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea and the Commercial Registration Act; and

WHEREAS, the founders and subscribers have subscribed in full for all issued shares and have paid the entire subscribed capital into a frozen pre-incorporation bank account, as evidenced by the bank's paid-in capital balance certificate; and

WHEREAS, notice of this organizational meeting has been duly given to all directors-elect, and all directors-elect are present or have waived notice in writing;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the board of directors, by unanimous consent, adopts the following corporate actions and statutory resolutions:

1. SUBSCRIPTION AND ISSUANCE OF SHARE CAPITAL. The board ratifies the subscription schedule, confirms the allocation of shares to each subscriber as set forth in the subscription records, and approves the issuance and payment of the entire share capital in the amount stated in the Articles of Incorporation. The Representative Director and Chief Financial Officer are authorized to collect the paid-in capital balance certificate, to execute share certificates, and to deliver share certificates to the subscribers following the completion of incorporation registration.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION AND PAYMENT RAILS. The board approves the opening and maintenance of corporate bank accounts, including domestic won accounts and foreign-currency settlement accounts, at recognized Korean commercial banks. The Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer are, jointly or with such signature matrix as approved by the board, authorized to execute all account opening forms, use online banking, approve and execute wire transfers, receive and settle funds through Stripe and PayPal, and complete foreign exchange transactions in compliance with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The board acknowledges that the Company's banking and anti-money-laundering risk tier is Medium-Risk Enhanced and directs management to implement client due diligence, transaction monitoring, and sanctions screening controls appropriate to online jewelry and timepiece sales.

3. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE. The board adopts the address identified in the Articles of Incorporation as the registered office of the Company within the jurisdictional territory of the Seoul Central District Court. The Chief Executive Officer is authorized to execute the lease or occupancy documents, to file the incorporation registration application with the competent court registry, and to receive statutory notices, tax correspondence, and service of process at the registered office.

4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. The board appoints the persons named in the officer acceptance forms to the following positions: the Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer, responsible for the general management, external representation and binding authority of the Company; the Chief Financial Officer and Inside Director, responsible for accounting and financial controls; and the Statutory Auditor (Gamsa), who shall supervise the directors' performance of duties and inspect corporate books as permitted by the Commercial Act. Each appointee accepts office and shall serve until the end of the first annual general meeting or until a successor is duly appointed.

5. GOVERNANCE, SEAL, AND COMPLIANCE INSTRUCTIONS. The board approves the creation and use of the corporate seal, the filing of business and tax registration with the National Tax Service, the submission of the online mail-order sales business notification under the Electronic Commerce Consumer Protection Act, the establishment of accounting books, and the delegation of tax filing obligations to licensed tax representatives. The Representative Director is further authorized to execute and deliver all documents required by the court registry, tax authorities, and financial institutions. The Chief Financial Officer is directed to implement internal controls, consumer-protection measures, and record-keeping procedures appropriate for the Company's e-commerce operations.

The board declares that this resolution is effective immediately and that it shall constitute binding corporate authorization for each action referenced above. This resolution may be presented in original, certified, or excerpted form as annexure to applications filed with governmental authorities.

UNANIMOUSLY ADOPTED by all directors at the organizational meeting on the date first written above.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Foundational Documents, Share Subscriptions, and Paid-in Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Korean commercial bank authorized to hold pre-incorporation subscription accounts; external corporate counsel.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Corporate counsel will draft the Articles of Incorporation, share subscription schedule, officer acceptance forms, and the first board resolution. Every subscriber must execute a share subscription agreement and pay the full subscription price by wire transfer or cash deposit into the Chusik Hoesa's temporary frozen subscription account opened by the incorporators under the Commercial Act. If the contribution is in kind, a statutory appraiser's appraisal report must be obtained and described in the Articles. No minimum capital is required, but the entire subscribed capital must be deposited and cannot be withdrawn until incorporation registration is completed. Following the deposit, the bank issues a paid-in capital balance certificate, which becomes a prerequisite for notarization and registration. The founding shareholders' identities, nationality, sanctions exposure, and beneficial ownership data must be screened to support subsequent Korean banking and anti-money-laundering compliance, given the Medium-Risk Enhanced profile.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation
Share subscription schedule and initial shareholder list
Executed share subscription agreements and payment orders
Bank paid-in capital balance certificate or equivalent proof of deposit
Identity documents and passports of each founder/subscriber
Power of attorney, if any, authenticated by a Korean consulate or apostille
Corporate counsel's legal opinion or engagement letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the deposit application or questions the source of funds, the incorporators shall supply enhanced due diligence documents, including bank statements, tax declarations, gift or inheritance verification, and a written explanation of the lawful source of funds. If the subscribed capital is insufficient, the founders shall execute a supplementary payment order and resubmit the paid-in capital certificate. Counsel will review and correct any deficiency in the subscription schedule and re-execute the affected documents before proceeding to notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public authorized under the Korean Notaries Act, within the district of the intended registered office (Seoul Central District).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founding shareholders or their duly authorized attorneys must appear before a Korean notary to verify identity and execute the final Articles of Incorporation. The notary will review the Articles to confirm that the mandatory provisions prescribed by the Commercial Act have been included, including the corporate name, purpose, registered office, issued shares, share par value and class, contribution method, paid-in capital schedule, officers, and auditor provisions. The notary also verifies the subscription statement and the paid-in capital balance certificate. After confirming compliance, the notary certifies the Articles and affixes the statutory notarial form. Certified copies are prepared for filing with the court registry, the district tax office, and the bank. Foreign shareholders executing by power of attorney must have the power of attorney notarized abroad and authenticated by a Korean consulate or apostilled unless exempted under Korean notarial practice.
required_dossiers: Final Articles of Incorporation (multiple certified originals)
Paid-in capital balance certificate
Subscriber identification documents and witnesses if required
Power of attorney and notarization of each foreign founder
Subscription schedule with share allotments
Corporate seal and representative officer's personal seal certificate if available
Payment receipt for notarial fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary suspends or refuses certification because of a noncompliant provision, the founders shall amend the Articles, convene a new subscriber consent meeting, and resubmit the corrected Articles for notarization. If a foreign power of attorney is rejected for lack of authentication, the applicant shall obtain an apostille or consular legalization and, if necessary, petition for re-execution before the notary. Any added notarial fees will be paid by the Company or the responsible subscriber as set out in the subscription agreement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration with the Seoul Central District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Bureau, Registration Division of the Seoul Central District Court (Korean Court Registration Office).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, counsel files the application for incorporation registration with the competent court registry based on the registered office address. The application must include the original notarized Articles of Incorporation, written acceptances of office signed by each director and statutory auditor, the share subscription schedule, the paid-in capital balance certificate, registered seal certificate for each statutory officer, lease agreement or owner consent, and the court registration tax payment receipt. The registrar examines legal compliance and verifies that the officers have executed valid acceptances. Upon approval, the court enters the company into the commercial register and issues the corporate registration certificate. The registration certificate, together with the certified Articles, is the principal legal evidence of the Company's existence and is required for opening bank accounts, tax registration, and licensing procedures.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (original and certified copies)
Application for registration of incorporation
Written acceptance of office by each director and auditor
Share subscription schedule and allotment sheet
Paid-in capital balance certificate from the bank
Registered seal certificate for each statutory officer and director
Lease agreement or owner's consent for registered office
Power of attorney for the filing agent
Court registration tax payment receipt
Identifications and corporate seal of the representative director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a request for supplementation, counsel shall cure the identified defect within the statutory response period, typically five to seven business days, by filing additional evidence such as a corrected Articles, renewed officer acceptance, or lease documentation. If the registration is refused on substantive grounds, the applicants may file an administrative appeal with the competent administrative court or apply for a new registration after correcting the deficiencies. If the delay is caused by court backlogs, counsel shall request expedited review and obtain a written receipt evidencing the filing date to preserve legal rights.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the National Tax Service and Online Mail-Order Sales Business Notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (local district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office) and the local Si/Gun/Gu district office responsible for consumer protection and e-commerce notifications.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty calendar days after issuance of the corporate registration certificate, the Company must file the business registration application with the competent local district tax office of the National Tax Service. The application requires the corporate registration certificate, registered office lease, representative director identification, corporate seal certificate, and the board resolution approving the business purpose. The tax office will assign a corporate business registration number and issue the business registration certificate (saeopja deungrokjeung), which enables VAT invoicing and corporate taxpayer identification. Simultaneously, because the Company is engaged in online retail under ISIC 4791, the Company must file the online mail-order sales business notification (Tongsin Panmae-eop Shingo) with the local Si/Gun/Gu office under the Electronic Commerce Consumer Protection Act. This notification must be completed before displaying advertised goods on the website or accepting third-party settlement through Stripe or PayPal. The notification submission includes the business registration number, e-commerce site domain, store-name, director details, customer-service contact information, and physical office address for consumer claims.
required_dossiers: Corporate registration certificate (deunggisajang-jeungmyeong)
Business registration application form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation or certified copy
Board resolution adopting business name and tax registration
Lease contract or office ownership verification
Corporate seal certificate and representative director identification
CEO and CFO identification documents
Online mail-order sales business notification form
Website or mobile commerce operational information and customer complaint contact details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office queries the application because of a mismatch in the business purpose code, the Company must submit an amended registration reflecting ISIC 4791 and NAICS 458310 and resubmit. If the local district office rejects the mail-order notification due to incomplete consumer-protection data, the Company must correct the deficiencies and resubmit within the designated cure period. In case of prolonged refusal, the Company may file an administrative appeal to the local authority's review body. The Company may not engage in e-commerce settlement until the notification is accepted and must temporarily suspend advertising if so directed by authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and Payment Gateway Merchant Registration with Stripe and PayPal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean commercial banking institution (e.g., Kookmin, Shinhan, Woori, or Hana Bank) and the merchant compliance departments of Stripe and PayPal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Representative Director and CFO shall appear at the corporate banking branch with the incorporation registration certificate, business registration certificate, corporate seal certificate, lease agreement, and the board resolution approving the account signature matrix. The bank will perform customer due diligence, verify the Company's beneficial owners, and require the completed corporate account application form. The account will be used for operating funds, VAT remittances, payroll, and settlement of payments received through Stripe and PayPal. After the account is opened, the Company applies for Stripe and PayPal merchant accounts by submitting the business registration certificate, business and bank address information, website content, product descriptions for fashion jewelry and fine timepieces, expected monthly transaction volumes, and the online mail-order sales notification number. Stripe and PayPal may request supply-chain invoices, trademark certificates, or watch and jewelry valuation information as part of their vetting process. The payment routing account must be verified through microdeposits or bank login confirmation.
required_dossiers: Corporate incorporation registration certificate
Business registration certificate
Corporate seal certificate (injamyeongjeung or injajungmyeong)
Board resolution authorizing bank accounts and merchant payment gateways
Representative director and CFO identification documents
Registered office lease or utility bill
Online mail-order sales business notification receipt or confirmation
Website URL and e-commerce platform details
Product catalog and pricing for jewelry/watches
Bank account proof required by Stripe or PayPal
Anti-money-laundering questionnaire and sanctions screening
Source of funds declarations when requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank imposes an enhanced due diligence condition due to the medium-risk e-commerce and jewelry category, the Company shall provide additional compliance documentation, including transaction projections, customer KYC procedures, product sourcing invoices, and AML policy. If Stripe or PayPal places a hold or requests verification, the Company must respond within seventy-two hours with bank statements, supplier invoices, and updated business documents. If the application is permanently terminated, the Company may proceed with a domestic Korean payment aggregator and reapply to global payment providers after establishing transaction history and strengthened compliance controls.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - ISIC 4791 is online retail of fashion jewelry and fine timepieces, not manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing under ISIC divisions 1xxx, 2xxx, 3xxx, 4xxx, or 52xx. No industrial licensing board or municipal manufacturing authority applies. The relevant consumer, tax, and e-commerce regulators are the National Tax Service, the local Si/Gun/Gu district office, and the Ministry of SMEs, and Startups for online sales support.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial or manufacturing operating permit is required. For online retail, the mandatory statutory notification is the Online Mail-Order Sales Business Report (Tongsin Panmae-eop Shingo) under the Electronic Commerce Consumer Protection Act, which is addressed in SOP Step 4. If the Company later adds a jewelry assembly, watch repair workshop, or physical warehouse, the applicable operation license would need to be assessed at that time.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - online retail under ISIC 4791 does not trigger the Korean Environmental Impact Assessment Act. The Ministry of Environment would become the competent agency only if a physical manufacturing, finishing, electroplating, jewelry-making, or chemical warehouse facility were established.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no full EIA report, environmental registration, or environmental consultation is required for an e-commerce company that only conducts internet sales and office-based administrative operations. The Company is required to comply with ordinary municipal waste collection, packaging disposal, and extended producer responsibility requirements under the Act on the Promotion of Saving and Recycling of Resources when supplying packaged goods.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - there are no process wastewater, industrial air emissions, volatile organic compounds, or hazardous waste streams generated by pure online retailing of watches and fashion jewelry. The Company must nonetheless comply with general standards regarding packaging waste, waste volume, and separation for recycling under the Waste Management Act. If a physical storage area or small assembly facility is added, the Company would need to assess effluent and VOC thresholds under the Clean Air Conservation Act and the Water Environment Conservation Act before operation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no civil defense fire permit is required for an online retail office and administrative location. A standard building occupancy certificate and the landlord's confirmation of compliance with the Korean Fire Safety Code should be retained. If the Company operates a merchandise stockroom, warehouse, or any area exceeding 100 square meters, or stores substantial quantities of combustible packaging, the local fire department will require a fire-fighting facility inspection and a business-use civil defense clearance under the Firefighting Facilities Installation, Maintenance, and Safety Control Act. An occupational safety and health duty under the Occupational Safety and Health Act arises as soon as the Company employs Korean workers; the CEO must file a workplace establishment report and retain a workplace health and safety manager where required by applicable thresholds.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, accessed through the HomeTax electronic tax administration portal at www.hometax.go.kr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a newly incorporated Chusik Hoesa (stock corporation), the statutory tax identification number is the 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN). After the company is registered with the Korean court registry, it must file a business registration application with the district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered place of business within 20 days of business commencement. A foreign non-resident entity engaging in VAT-liable activities in Korea without a Korean place of business must appoint a domestic tax representative in accordance with Article 53 of the Korean VAT Act. The tax representative then files a non-resident business registration application with the NTS district tax office, stating the foreign entity's legal name, registered address, description of the business, and the tax representative's details. Upon approval, the NTS issues a BRN and VAT registration number. A foreign corporation that maintains a Korean place of business or permanent establishment registers under the same standard BRN issuance procedure through its local branch or fixed place of business.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box pass-through election exists under Korean tax law for a Chusik Hoesa. A qualifying domestic parent and its wholly owned Korean subsidiaries may elect to file a consolidated corporate tax return under Article 76-17 of the Corporate Tax Act, provided the 100% ownership requirement is continuously satisfied from the beginning of the fiscal year. Certain professional service companies may elect the pass-through enterprise regime under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act, but a general e-commerce stock corporation selling jewelry and timepieces does not qualify. No election is available to treat a corporation as a simplified VAT taxpayer.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT exemption threshold is available. Every business operator must register for VAT with the district tax office within 20 days of business commencement. A simplified taxpayer regime applies only to individual business operators with annual taxable turnover below KRW 80,000,000; a Chusik Hoesa is always treated as a general taxpayer and must register regardless of projected turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All general VAT taxpayers, including every Chusik Hoesa, are required to issue electronic tax invoices (E-tax invoices) through the NTS HomeTax portal. Tax invoice details must be transmitted electronically to the NTS within the statutory filing period of the relevant VAT taxable period. Korea does not rely on a private digital stamping API or real-time clearance regime of the Latin American type; fiscal control is enforced through the mandatory electronic transmission of E-tax invoices, cash receipt issuance for consumer sales, and NTS data reconciliation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Korean VAT Act, exports of goods from the Republic of Korea are zero-rated. Zero-rating applies where the goods are delivered for export under a Korea Customs Service export declaration and actually depart the customs territory. Qualifying services include services supplied to non-residents, services connected with overseas property, and services performed wholly outside Korea. For an e-commerce seller of fashion jewelry and fine timepieces, the seller must evidence a genuine export transaction by retaining the customs export declaration, transport documentation confirming international movement of the goods, a commercial invoice, and order/payment records showing the customer is a non-resident and the goods were dispatched to a foreign address. For qualifying offshore digital services, additional evidence such as IP address records, customer service contracts, and service performance logs must be retained. Input VAT attributable to zero-rated exports is deductible and can be refunded via the VAT return mechanism.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
International Sales Contract or Purchase Order
Certificate of Foreign Exchange Acquisition (Korean equivalent of an Inward Remittance Certificate)
Proof of payment from the foreign buyer (if not covered by the foreign exchange certificate)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service jointly verify export zero-rating by reconciling export declarations, foreign exchange acquisition records, and the exporter's VAT returns. If the goods are found not to have physically left Korea, the foreign exchange proceeds are not repatriated within the statutory deadline, or the supporting export and foreign exchange documentation is missing or fraudulent, the NTS will reassess output VAT at 10%, impose additional tax penalties under the VAT Act (including aggravated penalties for intentional understatements), and claw back any input VAT previously refunded. Criminal liability may be pursued under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act for serious export VAT fraud. The statutory reassessment periods are up to five years for ordinary misreporting and ten years for unfiled returns or false/revenue-generating tax invoices.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with operational oversight delegated to licensed domestic foreign exchange banks and anti-money laundering supervision by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea maintains a predominantly liberalized foreign exchange regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, implemented by Bank of Korea and Ministry of Economy and Finance. Current account transactions, including e-commerce export receivables and trade settlement, are generally freely convertible and may be settled through Korean commercial banks without prior approval, although statistical reporting obligations remain. Capital account transactions are more tightly controlled: foreign direct investment, cross-border loans, and acquisition of securities require filings or approvals through a licensed foreign exchange bank or BOK. Dividends and profits of a Chusik Hoesa may be remitted abroad after the availability approach satisfies the foreign investment report and a bank verifies audited financial statements, tax clearance, and corporate resolution. The Korean won is exchangeable through the local interbank market; offshore KRW deliverability is restricted and non-resident access is channeled primarily through onshore bank accounts or NDFs. No general surrender obligation applies to export receipts; exporters can retain foreign currency, but must ensure settlement and reporting. The main hurdles for treasury are administrative rather than convertibility based, namely corporate KYC documentation, foreign investment registration, and proof of bona fide trade transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The standard statutory settlement period for export proceeds is six months from the date of export declaration. Where unavoidable commercial or force majeure circumstances prevent settlement within that period, the exporter or the foreign exchange bank may seek an extension of up to six months from BOK or the competent foreign exchange authority. There is no mandatory KRW conversion ratio applicable to export proceeds; exporters are permitted to retain 100% of export foreign currency receipts in a foreign currency deposit account, subject to foreign exchange notification and supporting export documentation. The mandatory conversion ratio is therefore effectively 0% to KRW, with 100% permitted offshore or onshore foreign currency retention.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Korean Won Basic Operational Currency Account and Foreign Currency Demand Deposit Account; Capital Escrow Account for inbound foreign equity investment
Korean Won Operating Account with Foreign Currency Corporate Settlement Account; dedicated escrow sub-account for capital injection
Basic Operational Currency Account, Foreign Currency Trade Account, and Capital Escrow Account for foreign direct investment proceeds
Korean Won Corporate Current Account, Foreign Currency Deposit Account, and Import/Export Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Low. Overseas financial-technology EMI providers such as Wise, Revolut Business, or Payoneer are not licensed as foreign exchange banks or deposit-taking institutions in South Korea. They cannot lawfully issue locally recognized KRW bank account equivalents, process statutory Korean FX reporting, or serve as the primary treasury clearing rail for a Korea-resident Chusik Hoesa. The Electronic Financial Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act restrict payment and foreign exchange business to authorized Korean financial institutions. A cross-border EMI may be used only as a supplemental collection conduit feeding into a tier-1 Korean bank account, not as the operational treasury account. For a corporate entity with Korean payroll, VAT, corporate tax, and customs obligations, a licensed Korean bank is mandatory for legal clearing and regulatory reporting.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean tier-1 banks generally require the statutory representative or an expressly authorized director, preferably one holding a Korean Alien Registration Card or a valid long-term visa, to appear physically at the branch for the initial corporate KYC interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not standard and is frequently rejected for foreign-owned corporations without prior Korean banking history. A notarized and apostilled power of attorney may be accepted for ongoing account administration, but the first account activation will require physical presence or, at most, a bank-approved video call verified by an existing face-to-face relationship. Recommended approach: at least one signing director must travel to Seoul for a one-to-two-day onboarding session with original corporate documents, corporate seal, government-issued identity documents, business registration certificate, and the foreign investment report confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign ownership opacity: non-resident shareholders or trusts hold voting rights in the Chusik Hoesa without a transparent natural-person UBO chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled certificate of incorporation and articles of incorporation; complete shareholder register; statutory declaration of ultimate beneficial owners identifying every natural person with direct or indirect control; passports or national identity cards of all shareholders and directors; official tax residence certificates; source-of-wealth documentation such as bank reference letters and asset statements; an organizational chart tracing the full ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce high-value goods red flags: jewelry and luxury watches create trade-based money laundering, invoice valuation fraud, and fragmented settlement through Stripe and PayPal.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction-level sales ledger for the first 12 months of operation; Stripe and PayPal payout reports with payout IDs mapped to bank statements; supplier invoices containing full names, business addresses, and product descriptions; customs import/export declarations and airway bills; independent appraisal or valuation certificates for items above USD 5,000; chargeback and refund logs; customer order history and delivery confirmation evidence for compliance-sampled payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between payment processor receivables and supplier trade payments may be interpreted as third-party funding, trade mispricing, or layering of illicit funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Reconciling schedule showing PSP gross receipts, fees, refunds, net payouts, and corresponding bank credits; signed contracts with Stripe and PayPal; supplier payment instructions executed via SWIFT and letters of credit; track-and-trace logistics evidence; general ledger extracts with VAT invoices; and a treasury memorandum explaining the commercial rationale for payment timing and currency routing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from foreign shareholders without a valid foreign investment report triggers Korean FX reporting and sanctions compliance scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign investment report confirmation or certificate issued by the foreign exchange bank or KOTRA under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; board resolution on share issuance and share subscription agreement; remittance slips for the foreign currency wire with the foreign investment registration reference; source-of-funds bank statements for the six months preceding the injection; sanctions screening results for the investor and the company; and notarized board minutes approving the capital contribution.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital for KR_CHUSIKHOESA must follow the Foreign Investment Promotion Act route. The foreign investor first files the foreign investment report through KOTRA or a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank; the bank then verifies the beneficiary Chusik Hoesa, issues the foreign investment registration or notification certificate, and opens an escrowed foreign currency account or accepts an SWIFT MT103 remittance into the company designated foreign currency account. The SWIFT payment must clearly reference the Korean entity legal name, the overseas investing company, and the foreign investment report/registration number in the remittance information field. The applicable Korean foreign exchange purpose code for direct investment in a Korean juridical person must be used. After receipt, the bank confirms the credited amount, performs foreign exchange notification to BOK/MOEF, and issues a capital verification acknowledgement. The funds may then be converted into KRW at the market rate through the onboarding bank, and the share capital or share premium must be recorded in the company register in accordance with the Korean Commercial Act.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade disbursements to international jewelry, watch, and fashion suppliers, the Chusik Hoesa should use SWIFT MT103 for open account and advance payment transactions, especially for payments below letter of credit thresholds. For high-value timepiece and fine jewelry inventory procurement, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit issued by the Korean bank is preferred, with at-sight commitment and presentation of commercial invoice, packing list, insurance certificate, and transport documents. Documentary collections are acceptable for mid-sized consignments with established suppliers. Each outbound payment must be matched to import documentation including the Korea Customs Service import declaration, supplier invoices, and logistics proof, and significant payments must be reported through the Korean foreign exchange information system. Trade settlement must stay within the statutory export and import payment periods, and the bank will require underlying trade evidence before processing each disbursement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable onshore KRW/USD and KRW/EUR forward contracts with licensed Korean foreign exchange banks, supported by the Chusik Hoesa measurable import and export exposure for jewelry, watches, and fashion goods.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on KRW with eligible global banks for offshore counterparties, limited to genuine commercial exposure and executed within BOK regulatory boundaries for non-resident settlement.
Cross-currency swaps between KRW, USD, and EUR where the notional is matched by verified trade receivables or payable contracts, with no naked or speculative swap positions.

Vanilla currency call and collar options on confirmed high-value trade invoices, subject to bank credit limits and foreign exchange reporting obligations, without leveraged speculative option structures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report and Financial Statements (Foreign Company Domestic Filing Equivalent for Chusik Hoesa)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) and Supreme Court Registry Office (Deung-gi-so)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the end of the fiscal year (fiscal year-end typically December 31, deadline March 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties up to 20% of unpaid corporate tax; additional per-month delinquency surcharge of 0.66% of underpaid tax after statutory deadline; repeated failure to file may trigger tax investigation and enforced collection, but does not directly administratively strike off the corporation; annual registration filing late fee of KRW 10,000 per day of delay, capped at KRW 100,000, plus potential court registry refusal and administrative fine

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Tax Reconciliation (Jurin Beobinse)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Cumulative filing deadline of March 31 for calendar-year corporations; corporations can file by April 30 if external tax accountant certifies the return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 20% of unpaid tax if filed within 6 months of deadline; 40% if filed after 6 months; monthly interest rate of 0.66% on unpaid corporate income tax for underreporting; possible seizure of bank accounts and business licenses; no automatic administrative strike-off for tax filing delinquency but commercial registry strike-off can follow extended failure to pay corporate taxes due to compulsory liquidation procedure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual FSS Foreign Exchange Reporting (Foreign Invested Company Status Change Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Federation of Banks (KFB) through designated foreign exchange bank; Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the end of the fiscal year for annual status reports; immediate filing within 30 days for any change to foreign investment status under Foreign Investment Promotion Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to KRW 1,000,000 per failure; possible reduction or loss of foreign investment benefits; repeated violations can lead to penalty surcharges and criminal fines up to KRW 20,000,000

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registration Renewal Certificate (Yeong- eop Deung-gi Annual Confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Supreme Court Registry Office (Deung-gi-so) via local district court registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual renewal should be confirmed by the last day of the fiscal year-end month anniversary; most registries accept filing by December 31 for calendar-year entities; for public corporations annual report confirmation due within 90 days after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Imposition of delinquency surcharge of KRW 10,000 per day up to KRW 100,000; failure to register changes might invalidate resolutions against third parties and expose directors to personal liability; continued failure can trigger ex-officio strike-off from the commercial register by court order under Commercial Act Article 520-2

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Local Business Tax Return and Property Tax Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual return due between May 1 and May 31 for business site location based on preceding year gross revenue; property tax due June 1 and December 1 for real estate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-payment penalty of 0.66% per month; negligence tax of 10-20% of unpaid local tax; seizure of business property; no automatic strike-off but local tax liens attach to registered assets

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax (VAT) Semi-Annual Returns (Two periodic filings)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half-year return due by July 25; second half-year return due by January 25; preliminary returns are based on actual VAT payable for the period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 10% of unpaid VAT for failure to pay within deadline; per-day interest 0.022% for improper return; 0.66% monthly additional collection surcharge; refusal to file can result in estimated assessment and business closure for habitual delinquents

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Withholding Tax Annual Return and Employer Certification of Wage Payments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual withholding statement on labor income due by March 10 of the following year; quarterly withholding remittances due by the 10th day of the month following each quarter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 10% for unfaithful withholding; 0.66% monthly delay interest; criminal penalty up to KRW 50,000,000 for willful non-collection; no strike-off but director liability for unpaid withheld national taxes

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies (Amendment effective 2019), an independent certified CPA audit is mandatory for any Chusik Hoesa meeting any of the following quantitative criteria: (1) total assets exceed KRW 12 billion (USD ~9 million) at fiscal year-end; (2) revenue exceeds KRW 10 billion (USD ~7.5 million) for the fiscal year; (3) total liabilities exceed KRW 7 billion (USD ~5.2 million); (4) number of employees exceeds 100; or (5) the company is a listed issuer on a Korean securities exchange regardless of size. Additionally, a smaller Chusik Hoesa with assets under KRW 12 billion may still be required to obtain a certified audit if it has more than 2,000 shareholders, if it is a financial institution, or if it is deemed sufficiently important by the Financial Services Commission. For unlisted companies with assets between KRW 10 billion and KRW 12 billion, a reduced review (not full audit) may apply under certain transition rules, but any company that is an SME with total assets below KRW 10 billion can qualify for exemption. Detailed thresholds are revised by the Financial Services Commission and Securities and Futures Commission under the Korean IFRS roadmap.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for entities required to conduct external audits; Generally Accepted Accounting Principles for non-public entities (Korean GAAP) for SMEs not requiring external audit; supervisory standards from the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants (KICPA); financial statements must be prepared in Korean Won (KRW) and accompany director and auditor reports.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Act on Financial Information and Use of Financial Information and the Specific Financial Information Act (Kamjeonggeum), foreign companies and Korean corporations must maintain up-to-date beneficial ownership information in their statutory corporate registers. There is no standalone annual UBO confirmation form for ordinary private companies; instead, every corporate resolution, share transfer, and director change must be filed with the Supreme Court Registry within 30 days. For banks and financial institutions, annual UBO confirmation is embedded in customer due diligence and must be refreshed at least annually. For a standard Chusik Hoesa, each actual share transfer must be recorded in the register of members and a verified registry filing must be submitted within 30 days, with penalties for false declarations under the Commercial Act; the company must also file a Beneficial Ownership Declaration with the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) when the company executes high-value real estate transactions, when obtaining bank financing, or when shareholding changes reach reporting thresholds. Failure to file within 30 days results in administrative fines of up to KRW 20,000,000 per event.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Board of Directors Meetings
Statutory Accounting Ledger and Inventory Ledger

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 1,200 per year for a corporate registered address and professional agent service in Seoul (including annual commercial registry renewal)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 15,000 for a certified external audit of an e-commerce jewelry and watches company with gross revenue between USD 1 million and USD 10 million; USD 15,000 - USD 40,000 if full K-IFRS audit and group consolidation applies

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22% (headline national marginal corporate income tax rate on taxable income exceeding KRW 3 billion; 10% up to KRW 200 million and 20% from KRW 200 million to KRW 3 billion)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Korean Small and Medium Enterprise (SME) may retain the 10% rate on the first KRW 200 million of taxable income; R&D tax credits are available up to 25%-50% for qualifying e-commerce software development; job creation tax deductions and temporary investment tax credits apply; free economic zone and foreign-investment promotion incentives may provide limited corporate tax holidays; no patent box regime exists for jewelry or fashion trademarks, but qualifying digital platform R&D is deductible and creditable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (법인세과세표준 및 세액계산서) submitted via Korea National Tax Service HomeTax E-Filing Portal; Form 101 and accompanying explanatory schedules
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The corporate income tax return and self-assessment payment are due within 3 months after the close of the fiscal year; for a December 31 year-end Chusik Hoesa, the deadline is March 31 of the following year; the deadline may be extended to 4 months for certain foreign-invested enterprises and for companies with overseas branches approved by the National Tax Service.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity identification: registered corporate name, business registration number (사업자등록번호), tax period, principal place of business, and representative director details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Korean Corporate Registration Number and confirm that the Chusik Hoesa is duly registered as a foreign-invested enterprise if non-resident shareholders hold equity. Attach the Schedule of Non-Resident Shareholders showing each shareholder's legal name, jurisdiction, and foreign tax identification number; failure to attach may trigger non-resident withholding penalties at the 22% statutory rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity classification and e-commerce merchant information: Korean Standard Industrial Classification code corresponding to ISIC 4791, online retail platform name, payment gateways (Stripe, PayPal), and whether the company is a high-value goods seller.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the KSIC code for online retail of jewelry, watches, and fashion goods. Clearly identify cross-border B2C sales and the territory of final retail customers. For non-resident shareholders managing overseas sales through foreign payment rails, the company must maintain a full revenue reconciliation to support Korean-source income declarations and avoid an export omission adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net income before tax per Korean IFRS/K-GAAP: gross revenue from online jewelry/watch sales, cost of goods sold, selling and administrative expenses, and operating income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjust accounting income for intercompany transactions with non-resident affiliates. Add back the non-deductible portion of royalties, commissions, and service fees paid to offshore related parties unless supported by arm's length documentation. Also add back entertainment expenses exceeding statutory caps and any fines or penalties. Maintain a transaction-by-transaction ledger for every Stripe and PayPal settlement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments reconciling accounting profit to taxable profit: items to add back (non-deductible expenses, excess reserves, gift and entertainment excess) and items to deduct (tax-exempt interest, dividend receiving deduction, and special reserves).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-owned Chusik Hoesa, apply the thin capitalisation rules: interest paid to a foreign controlling shareholder is non-deductible to the extent that the debt-equity ratio exceeds 3:1 (or 2:1 for financial institutions). Intercompany service fees must meet the benefit test and cannot be deducted if the service is duplicative of functions performed by the Korean entity. Ensure that no dividends paid to foreign shareholders are deducted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the taxable base (과세표준): accounting income less estimated deductions, loss carryforwards, and tax-exempt income adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 10-year tax loss carryforward period in accordance with Article 45(4) of the Corporate Tax Act. If the company was incorporated as a shell and later activated, the tax authority may deny loss carryforwards if there was no real continued business. For foreign branch losses, confirm under the applicable tax treaty whether they may be set off against Korean domestic taxable income; generally they may not be deducted unless the DTA expressly permits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of progressive corporate income tax rates to the taxable base and calculation of the national corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply: 10% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 20% on taxable income from KRW 200 million to KRW 3 billion; 22% on taxable income exceeding KRW 3 billion. Non-resident shareholders do not receive a crossed rate. The tax authority may recompute the base upward if transfer pricing adjustments are made under Article 52 of the Corporate Tax Act, so the return must be internally consistent with the TP documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and offsets: R&D credits, job creation credits, foreign tax credit for foreign-source income, and prior-year prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Korean entity derived foreign-source income and paid foreign withholding tax to third countries, a per-country foreign tax credit may be claimed on the corporate return, subject to the limitation under Article 57 of the Corporate Tax Act. The foreign tax credit must be computed in KRW using the exchange rate prevailing at the date of payment. Attach evidence of foreign tax payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final non-resident dividend, interest, and royalty withholding tax computation imposed on distributions and payments to non-resident shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Chusik Hoesa as a domestic corporation must withhold 22% (20% national corporate income tax plus 2% local income surtax) from dividends paid to non-resident shareholders unless a lower treaty rate applies. To apply the DTA rate, the payor must collect the foreign shareholder's Tax Residency Certificate and a beneficial ownership declaration before the dividend payment date, and submit the treaty rate application form to the National Tax Service. If the reduced rate is not timely verified, the excess withholding can be reclaimed through a tentative refund procedure. The remittance is due by the 10th day of the month following the month in which the tax is withheld.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable and settlement: total tax computed less interim prepayments, tax credits, and withheld salary/wage taxes; the net corporate income tax to be paid with the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the semi-annual interim prepayments with the final tax. Underpayments due to manipulated transfer pricing are subject to the additional tax equal to 10%-20% of the adjusted income, plus daily late payment interest of 0.022%. Double-check that the amount of non-resident withholding tax shown on the return is reflected in the monthly withholding remittance statements filed earlier. Any mismatch will initiate an NTS audit trigger for non-resident tax avoidance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory attachments: Schedule of International Related-Party Transactions, Local File/Master File certification, audit reports, and treaty benefit application forms.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When international related-party transactions exceed the KRW 50 billion threshold, the return must be accompanied by the completed TP Local File and Master File, or a written statement that the CVD? standard exemption applies. For DTA claim, attach the original Tax Residency Certificate, beneficial ownership statement, and the certificate of residence confirmation issued by the foreign tax authority. The NTS can reject the treaty if the documentation is incomplete or if the board of directors cannot demonstrate the economic substance of the Korean entity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without just cause triggers an additional tax under Article 47-2 of the Framework Act on National Taxes equal to 20% of the underpaid amount (40% for fraudulent concealment). Non-payment or underpayment accrues daily interest of 0.022%. Failure to file transfer pricing documentation may lead to a nominal fine of KRW 20 million plus a 10%-20% adjustment penalty assessed on the transfer pricing adjustment. Criminal tax evasion is punishable under Article 16(1) of the Act on Punishment of Tax Crimes by imprisonment up to 3 years or a fine up to KRW 100 million; fraudulent failure to withhold non-resident tax makes the company and its representative jointly liable for the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national withholding corporate income tax plus 2% local income surtax; reduced to 0%-15% for dividends under many Korean bilateral tax treaties, e.g., 10% U.S. treaty, 15% generally under UN model treaties).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced withholding tax rate under a Korea DTA, the non-resident shareholder must submit to the Korean paying company, before the dividend payment, (1) an original Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the competent foreign tax authority, indicating the shareholder is a resident and beneficial owner, (2) a completed beneficial ownership declaration using National Tax Service Form for treaty rate application, and (3) evidence of the shareholder's right to the dividend under the relevant commercial register. The Korean company must verify the TRC covers the calendar year of the distribution, retain the document in its tax records, and file the treaty rate application form together with the corporate income tax return. The withholding agent may apply the treaty rate only after the TRC has been received; otherwise it must withhold at 22% and the foreign shareholder may apply for a refund through the National Tax Service within the statutory limitation period (generally 3 years). For dividends channeled through a third-country intermediary, the beneficial ownership condition will be denied, and the full statutory 22% applies plus potential interest on unpaid amounts.

stage_6.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic law imposes 22% (20% national plus 2% local) withholding on royalties and interest paid to non-residents. Under Korean DTAs, the rates are often reduced to 10% or 15% for royalties and 10% for interest, depending on the counterparty jurisdiction (e.g., 15% for royalties under many recent protocols, 10% for banking interest). To claim the lower rate, the same TRC, beneficial ownership declaration, and payer-side procedural requirements as for dividends must be satisfied. Royalty payments to a non-resident in a favourable IP-holding jurisdiction without economic substance are subject to Article 91 of the Framework Act anti-avoidance, and the royalty may be disallowed if the recepient has no actual CIGA.
